title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Measurement properties of anhedonia-related patient-reported outcome measures in depression-related populations: A COSMIN systematic review.
authors: Wang Q, Cui Y, Yao Z, Wu Z, Zhao X
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anhedonia is central to depressive disorders, but evidence on anhedonia-related patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) has not been systematically synthesized using COSMIN. METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycInfo, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 1 May 2026. COSMIN methods and PRISMA-COSMIN guidance informed the assessment of measurement properties, evidence certainty, and recommendations. RESULTS: Twenty-five articles covering 28 instrument-level evaluations and 69 cohorts (58 adult, 11 adolescent) assessed 10 PROM families. Both English and Chinese adult DARS versions were Category A; other adult PROMs were Category B. For adolescents, the English Anhedonia Scale for Adolescents (ASA) was Category An under a developmental framework, whereas the Chinese ASA and DARS-Adolescent were Category B. Under strict DSM/ICD-defined clinical depression criteria, both DARS versions remained Category A, while both ASA versions were Category B. No PROM had high-certainty evidence across all nine measurement properties, and none was Category C. LIMITATIONS: Direct high-certainty clinical evidence was limited, and studies varied by population, language, setting, and instrument version. CONCLUSIONS: DARS was the most comprehensively supported adult PROM. The English ASA is recommended for adolescents under a developmental framework; Chinese adolescent measures need further qualitative validation. Reliability, measurement error, cross-cultural validity, and meaningful-change thresholds require further study. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251142590.

title: The effects of an online mindfulness-based intervention for parents of children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
authors: Zhang ZJ, Lo HHM, Cheung RYM, Chen Q, Yeung WT, Chan SKC, Au A, Wong EWY
abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have been identified as a complementary treatment for children with ADHD. While there is a growing interest in developing MBIs in online formats, its application in parents is largely based on healthy populations. A two-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) was designed to investigate the effectiveness of an online MBI (arm 1) compared with an online psychoeducation (PSY) program (arm 2). Outcomes were measured before the intervention, after the intervention, and at 3-month follow-up. A total of 248 parents whose children with ADHD symptoms aged 6 to 12 years old participated in the study, with 131 parents assigned to the online MBI group and 117 to the PSY group. Both groups indicated significant and lasting improvements in their children's ADHD symptoms, executive functioning, and parental well-being. In addition, parental stress levels and two dimensions of expressed emotion, including critical comments and initial statements, decreased significantly in both groups. Notably, a specific benefit of the online MBI was identified for insomnia. A small-magnitude improvement in parent-child relationship quality, as a dimension of expressed emotion, was observed in the repeated measures ANOVA but was not consistently supported by the sensitivity analysis. Future studies should verify the specific and sustainable treatment effects of MBIs, strengthening parental engagement and support.

title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging.
authors: Oliveira GM, Nunes BP, Lam K, Lima-Costa MF, Torres JL, Macinko J, Moreira BS, Avelino-Silva TJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants' usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. FINDINGS: Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p < 0.001 for hospitalization). In the public system, higher primary care effectiveness attenuated the association between multimorbidity and hospitalization (interaction prevalence ratio [PR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.63-0.87). In contrast, in the private system, higher primary care effectiveness strengthened the associations of multimorbidity with ED visits (interaction PR = 1.40, 95% CI = 1.18-1.66) and hospitalization (interaction PR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.22-2.50). INTERPRETATION: Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. FUNDING: The Brazilian National Council for Scientific and Technological Development, the Alzheimer's Association, and the National Institute on Aging.

title: Advancing neonatal care through non-invasive biochemical monitoring and diagnostics.
authors: Son H, Kim D, Yeo WH, Lim HR
abstract: Repeated blood sampling remains the basis of neonatal biochemical assessment, although it is painful and, in extremely preterm infants, removes close to one third of the circulating blood volume. Non-invasive biosensing offers alternatives, but most studies report analytical figures of merit or correlation with blood, which do not show whether a measurement meets the requirements of clinical use. This review maps neonatal biomarkers to saliva, sweat, tears, urine, and exhaled breath and to electrochemical, optical, and chemiresistive platforms, and compares their technical progress with the requirements of clinical use. Adapting established test-evaluation methodology, we define the evidence required for replacement, triage, add-on, monitoring, discovery, and diagnosis with matrix-native thresholds, and we add requirements specific to non-invasive matrices: sampling failure, variable matrix-to-blood ratios, and matrix confounders. Neonatal data show that the same statistic can lead to opposite conclusions, as salivary caffeine and C-reactive protein illustrate. Only sweat chloride and transcutaneous bilirubin are established in routine neonatal practice. Among representative custom-engineered devices, the evidence mostly stops at paired comparison in selected, case-control, or balanced samples, and performance in consecutively enrolled infants is rarely reported. For small molecules and electrolytes, progress now depends more on study design, namely consecutive enrollment and paired sampling at clinically indicated blood draws, than on further gains in analytical sensitivity. Extending the framework to early-life protection, we argue that a measurement protects an infant only when it detects change in time for an effective intervention, and that this chain is so far best supported within established screening pathways.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface.
authors: Sun L, Zhang J, Abdullah CN, Shen Y, Geng S, Xu S, Zhou J
abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal "spatial paradox" challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase PaCrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting PaCrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ, label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust PaCrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER-LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.

title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
authors: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D, He K, Chen Y, Li Y, Dai S, He Y
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for adverse perinatal outcomes; rapid and accurate detection is crucial for preventing maternal-neonatal transmission and for guiding clinical interventions. Current GBS detection methods are limited by long assay times, insufficient sensitivity, and high equipment and operational requirements, restricting their application in resource-limited settings and rapid detection scenarios. Targeting the cfb gene of GBS, this study developed ERA-CasMNPs by integrating enzymatic recombinase amplification (ERA), CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated specific recognition and trans-cleavage activity of ssDNA, and horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-modified magnetic nanoparticle complexes (MNPs)-based colorimetric signal output. The ERA-CasMNPs biosensor enables rapid and sensitive visual detection of GBS within 85 min, with an LOD95 of 23.3 copies/μL (95% confidence interval: 15.6-34.8 copies/μL). Moreover, evaluation using 135 cultured clinical bacterial isolates demonstrated that ERA-CasMNPs achieved a sensitivity of 97.33%, a specificity of 98.33%, and a detection accuracy of 97.78%, comparable to qPCR. These results indicate that the ERA-CasMNPs biosensor provides a sensitive and visual method for rapid detection of GBS and supports its potential for further evaluation in resource-limited and rapid-testing settings.

title: Atypical early-life ultrasonic vocalizations disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad in the BTBR model of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Cofsky NI, Binder MS
abstract: Alterations in early-life communication are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). While these deficits are well conserved in mouse models, few studies have assessed how aberrations in neonatal vocalizations affect maternal behaviors and disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad. To better elucidate the consequences of altered communication in ASD models, we assessed ultrasonic vocalization (USV) production in pups and the corresponding retrieval behaviors in dams using C57 and BTBR (autistic-like) mice. We first used the pup's dam as the retriever and found that BTBR dams retrieved significantly fewer pups than C57 dams. We then used a novel C57 dam as the retriever and found that BTBR pups were retrieved significantly slower than C57 pups. Follow-up analyses detected positive correlations between call duration and retrieval time and amplitude and retrieval time in BTBR pups. Similarly, we found that C57 mice that were retrieved the fastest had calls of a lower amplitude than slowly retrieved mice. In the BTBR model, we found that faster retrieved mice produced shorter calls with a higher pitch than slowly retrieved mice, displaying call characteristics more similar to C57 pups. Lastly, we found that a more diverse call type repertoire was associated with a faster retrieval time. Overall, our study demonstrates that altered USV production significantly affects the pup-dam communication dyad. Furthermore, we identified the USV duration, amplitude, and a more diverse call type repertoire as being critical factors underlying maternal retrieval.

title: Integrated metabolic and process engineering of Rhodotorula toruloides for light-driven hydrocarbon production.
authors: Zhao H, Zhang Y, Lyu L, Lu H, Zhao ZK
abstract: Long-chain hydrocarbons are bulky chemicals traditionally produced via petroleum refining. Microbial production of these hydrocarbons from renewable resources has attracted much attention, but is limited by precursor accessibility and catalysis efficiency. Here, we combined genetic engineering and photobioprocess optimization for blue-light-driven hydrocarbon production by the oleaginous yeast Rhodotorula toruloides. Cytosolic expression of the Chlorella variabilis fatty acid photodecarboxylase (CvFAP) in R. toruloides conferred cells producing 15.0 mg/L hydrocarbons, while targeting CvFAP to lipid droplets (LDs) via fusion with the LD-associated protein Ldp1 enhanced titer by more than 3-fold. Systematic optimization of blue-light fermentation further doubled hydrocarbon titers. Metabolic rewiring of the pathways related to fatty acid activation, lipid turnover, and carotenoid biosynthesis showed that CRT1 deletion had the most pronounced effect, increasing hydrocarbon titer by 2.5-fold. Additional improvements were achieved by reinforcing free fatty acid supply and increasing CvFAP copy number. The final strain R. toruloides NF72D produced 557.7 mg/L hydrocarbons in flask culture, over 37-fold higher than that by the initial cytosolic expression strain. Collectively, this study demonstrates the importance of proper localization of key enzymes for improved biosynthesis of fatty acid-derived metabolites and a great potential for light-driven production of renewable hydrocarbons by oleaginous yeasts.

title: Systematic metabolic engineering for trans-aconitic acid production in Aspergillus niger.
authors: Wang S, He J, Li W, Cui C, Liu J, Liu H
abstract: Trans-aconitate (TAA) is a valuable bio-based chemical for nematicides and polymer synthesis. We repurposed the industrial citrate producer Aspergillus niger for efficient TAA biosynthesis. Heterologous AexA enabled extracellular aconitate export. However, overexpressing aconitases from various sources, targeted to the cytoplasm or mitochondria, failed to increase titers. Although mitochondria proved the optimal site for cis-aconitate accumulation, the bottleneck likely persisted due to thermodynamic constraints. To overcome this, we designed a push-pull strategy: a pull module using mitochondrial MttA to export cis-aconitate to the cytosol, where TbrA isomerizes it to TAA, coupled with a push module enhancing cytosolic acetyl-CoA via the phosphoketolase pathway. Multicopy tbrA expression was critical. The final strain produced 34.30 g/L total aconitate (>90% TAA) in a 5-L bioreactor within 6 days. This work highlights a compartmentalized push-pull strategy exploiting mitochondrial-cytosolic organization to convert a citrate chassis into a high-yield TAA cell factory.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
authors: Liu H, Li X, Li M, Jiu J, Zhao Y, Li D, Zhang J, Yan L
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

title: Sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride/cerium tungstate nanocomposites for ultrasensitive dopamine sensing in mouse striatal tissue.
authors: Jang HG, Manikandan R, Moon SM, Mugunthan UA, Lee J, Kang GW, Park J, Yoon JH
abstract: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for rapid diagnostic tools for the highly specific and sensitive detection of disease-related biomarkers has increased significantly. Hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable screen-printed electrodes have shown remarkable potential for the electrochemical biosensing of various biomarkers. This study reports the fabrication of a hybrid nanocomposite comprising sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride (S-g-C3N4) nanosheets integrated with two-dimensional cerium tungstate (CeW) for highly sensitive electrochemical dopamine detection. The synthesized S-g-C3N4@CeW hybrid nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and electrochemical measurements. Electroanalytical performance was evaluated using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) under optimized experimental conditions. The fabricated electrochemical sensor exhibited a wide linear concentration range for dopamine from 0.1 to 500 μM, with a low detection limit of 1.13 nM and high sensitivity of 151.69 μA μM-1 cm-2. Finally, the fabricated sensor was used for the ex-vivo determination of dopamine in Parkinson's disease-induced mouse striatum-tissue samples, achieving good accuracy with recovery rates of 92.0 to 101.4%. This study demonstrates a promising strategy for fabricating hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable electrochemical sensors for neurotransmitter detection in animal-disease models.

title: Sex-divergent vulnerability to chronic peripheral LPS challenge in aged ApoE4 mice: Male systemic fragility versus female central neuroinflammation.
authors: Barberà-Parada S, Biosca-Brull J, Gabaldón-Díaz R, Rodulfo-Cárdenas R, Guardia-Escoté L, Blanco J, Cabré M, Colomina MT
abstract: Inflammageing links chronic inflammation to biological aging, contributing to senescence and multimorbidity common in the elderly. In neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory processes play a causal role in accelerating neurodegeneration. Interestingly, apolipoprotein E (APOE), particularly the APOEε4 allele, is a major genetic risk factor for neurodegeneration, acting as a key immunomodulator with sex differences. This is especially relevant given the lack of clear prevention strategies for APOEε4 carriers. Therefore, this study characterized the sex-specific neuroinflammatory and cognitive vulnerability of APOE4 genotype under a chronic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in senescence-transition stage. Male and female homozygous apoE4 mice (15-16 months old) were administered intraperitoneal doses of 0 or 0.25 mg/kg LPS three times per week for a total of 17 doses. Body weight was monitored, and behavioural assessments were conducted from the 12th injection until the 17th. Serum and tissues were collected to assess hippocampal, cortical and systemic markers of inflammation, antioxidant-related genes, genes implied in myelin dynamics, and neurotrophin-related transcripts. Findings revealed basal sex-dependent divergent phenotypes with specific responses under LPS challenge. Under LPS treatment, males exhibited higher systemic fragility, with significantly increased mortality, which may have conditioned cognitive outcomes. Females showed greater central alterations related to neuroinflammation along with altered expression of myelin-related transcripts. However, the results suggest a stablished tolerance to LPS. These results highlight how chronic systemic inflammation during ageing in an APOE4 genotype background shapes sex-divergent pathological trajectories, underscoring the need to address sex-specific therapeutic strategies.

title: DA-S2RL: Disease-aware shared-specific representation learning for heterogeneous image-EHR Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
authors: Wang W, Shi Y, Cheng J, Liu Y
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Combining electronic health records (EHR) with medical images is important for improving the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, neuroimages and EHR differ greatly in semantic content and data distribution. Neuroimages mainly reflect brain structure and metabolic abnormalities, while EHR records clinical symptoms and behavioral changes. Directly fusing these heterogeneous modalities may mix shared disease information with modality-specific diagnostic cues, resulting in redundant and ambiguous representations. To address this problem, we propose DA-S2RL, a disease-aware shared-specific multimodal representation learning framework for AD diagnosis. DA-S2RL organizes heterogeneous image and EHR features into disease-related shared semantics and modality-specific diagnostic residuals. The core of DA-S2RL is the shared-specific cross-modal coding (SCC) module. It strengthens cross-modal semantic consistency, suppresses redundant correlations, and enables mutual refinement between shared semantics and diagnostic residuals. Before SCC, image features are integrated into a compact image representation, and EHR features are encoded into the same feature space. Experiments on ADNI and NACC demonstrate that explicitly organizing heterogeneous image-EHR representations into shared disease semantics and modality-specific residuals improves multimodal diagnostic learning under different image-EHR settings.

title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
authors: Wang Z, Su Y, Zhang S, Yu B, Wei Y, Liu H, Veselova IA, Lv S
abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8+ T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging.
authors: Wu JW, Wang YK, Mukundan A, Karmakar R, Nhu NNQ, Nagisetti Y, Liao WC, Han ML
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, image-based exploratory feasibility study to descriptively evaluate the diagnostic performance of WLI, NBI, and SAVE. A dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images (450 each for WLI, NBI, and SAVE) across normal mucosa, dysplasia, and ESCC stages from 158 patients was blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and reading time. RESULTS: For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of WLI and NBI in this exploratory dataset, but lacked sensitivity for dysplasia. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further prospective, multicenter validation to refine the algorithm for early cancer detection.

title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
authors: Inaba K, Motomura M, Azuma Y, Kimoto T, Takahashi H, Ueo T, Narita R, Tada K
abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype.
authors: Ohno K, Nakatani E, Kurokami T, Kawai A, Matsuda M, Masui Y, Satoh T, Hirata T
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence. RESULTS: Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Long-term Endoscopic Evolution of a Pyloric Gland Adenoma Arising in Nonatrophic Gastric Mucosa and Initially Resembling a Fundic Gland Polyp.
authors: Kobayashi R, Nakanishi H, Takaura K, Tanaka S, Maeyashiki C, Tamaki N, Yasui Y, Sakurai U
abstract: Pyloric gland adenoma (PGA) is a rare gastric epithelial neoplasm often associated with autoimmune or metaplastic atrophic gastritis. An 80-year-old man underwent serial upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. A small gastric fundus lesion initially resembling a fundic gland polyp (FGP) was followed without biopsy. Over 11 years, it enlarged to 22 mm and became increasingly whitish, against a background described endoscopically as nonatrophic. Biopsy suggested PGA, and the lesion was resected en bloc by endoscopic submucosal dissection. Closely packed pyloric-type glands showed elongation, tortuosity, branching, and cystic dilatation, with diffuse MUC6 expression and MUC5AC expression restricted to the surface epithelium. The lesion was diagnosed as PGA with low-grade dysplasia. The adjacent oxyntic mucosa showed no atrophy, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, or nodular enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia. Without an initial biopsy, whether the lesion was already PGA or developed within a pre-existing FGP remains unknown. An enlarging or increasingly whitish FGP-like lesion warrants histologic assessment, even in nonatrophic gastric mucosa.

title: Hybrid nanovesicle artificial antigen-presenting cells integrate endogenous tumor antigen display with senescence-mimetic erythrocyte membrane-directed splenic T-cell priming.
authors: Yang Z, Li S, Guo Y, Wang T, Han H, Ma M, Zhang Y, Tang W
abstract: Artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) provide a non-genetic approach to T-cell activation, but their in vivo performance is often limited by predefined peptide-major histocompatibility complex class I (pMHC-I) repertoires and inefficient delivery to secondary lymphoid organs. Here, we engineer senescence-derived hybrid nanovesicles that integrate endogenous antigen display and organ-directed trafficking within a single membrane material. Nanovesicles derived from senescent cancer cells retain increased levels of endogenously generated pMHC-I complexes, whereas nanovesicles derived from senescence-mimetic red blood cells confer spleen-directed biodistribution. Fusion of these membranes generates SS-hNVs, which are further functionalized with anti-CD28 and interleukin-2 to form SS-aAPCs that provide coordinated T-cell receptor (TCR), costimulatory, and cytokine signals. Hybrid membrane composition governs splenic accumulation and CD8+ T-cell engagement following intravenous administration. SS-aAPCs expand antigen-specific CD8+ T cells and TCF-1+PD-1+ progenitor-like populations, enhance cytotoxic responses, and suppress tumor growth in B16-OVA and MC38 models. Combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) blockade further improves tumor control. By assigning endogenous antigen display and lymphoid trafficking to distinct source membranes, this platform establishes a structure-function strategy for constructing systemically administered aAPCs. These findings support that physiologically remodeled membranes can be assembled as modular biomaterials to coordinate molecular immune signaling with organ-level biodistribution, enabling in vivo T-cell priming without predefined epitope loading or genetic modification of immune cells.

title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors.
authors: Gong L, Wang X, Zheng Y, Liu S, Zhang F, Sun Y, Qi Y, Han L
abstract: Metabolic therapies targeting tumor amino acid dependence, represented by asparaginase (ASNase), have shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, owing to poor stability, low penetration, and high immunogenicity. Here, we design a thermosensitive tumor-targeted ASNase fusion protein (ASNase-ELP-LHRH) via AlphaFold2, by integrating elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) and luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH), to overcome these drawbacks. ELP drives in situ depot formation, extending half-life to ∼400 h (95-fold increase) and reducing anti-ASNase antibody levels 70-fold. LHRH mediates receptor-dependent tumor targeting and deep penetration. ASNase-ELP-LHRH achieves persistent asparagine (Asn) depletion, counteracting metabolic adaptation to induce nutrient starvation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, the construct blocks metastasis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition through downregulating Twist1 and upregulating E-cadherin, effectively inhibiting lung metastasis for 25 days in triple-negative breast cancer models. We further observed time-dependent changes in CD8+ T-cell effector-marker expression under Asn deprivation, characterized by dynamic alterations in IFN-γ and granzyme B expression. Combined with anti-PD-L1, this achieves a "dual boost" of antitumor immunity, durably inhibiting metastasis for 40 days and extending survival 1.5-fold. The modular ligand-exchangeable platform offers a generalizable strategy for protein optimization and establishes ASNase-ELP-LHRH as a promising metabolic-immunotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, bridging protein engineering, tumor metabolism and cancer immunology.

title: Ultrasensitive direct detection of HMGB1 protein via covalently modified graphene field-effect transistors.
authors: Aznar Y, Azpeitia J, Mompéan F, Telle HH, Blanco Y, León-Boigues L, Hernández-Sánchez C, de la Rosa EJ
abstract: High-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) is a nuclear chromatin-binding protein that can be released into the extracellular milieu during cellular stress or necrosis, or be actively secreted, where it acts as an early pro-inflammatory mediator implicated in a broad spectrum of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. Extracellular HMGB1 is therefore an attractive clinical biomarker for health conditions involving necrosis or extensive tissue damage. In this work, we present the development and characterization of a covalently modified graphene field-effect transistor (CG-FET) incorporating a DNA aptamer for the ultrasensitive detection of HMGB1. The device was fabricated using a commercially available anti-HMGB1 DNA aptamer and its successive functionalization steps were independently validated by micro-particle-induced X-ray emission (μ-PIXE). Electrical measurements were performed to monitor the changes in the graphene Dirac point throughout the functionalization process and HMGB1 binding. The sensor exhibited clear and reproducible analytical performance, enabling detection of the target protein with limits of detection (LoDs) in the attomolar range. Specificity studies confirmed selective aptamer-HMGB1 recognition and demonstrated that optimized buffer conditions reduce nonspecific interactions. These results demonstrate the performance of the CG-FET biosensor based on a commercially available aptamer and provide a basis for its further development and validation in complex biological matrices towards potential diagnostic applications.

title: The influence of visual restriction and lower-limb proprioception on walking capacity in children with and without upper motor neuron lesions.
authors: Marsico P, Meier L, Buchmann A, Kläy A, van Hedel HJA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gait stability depends on the integration of visual and proprioceptive feedback. Children with upper motor neuron (UMN) lesions often exhibit proprioceptive deficits; however, the interaction between these deficits and visual input during walking remains unclear. This study investigated the influence of visual restriction and lower-limb proprioceptive function on walking capacity in children with UMN lesions compared to typically developing (TD) peers. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 42 children with UMN lesions and 49 TD peers completed the 10-Meter Walk Test under normal and reduced visual conditions. We calculated absolute and relative (reduced vision/normal vision) gait capacity metrics. Proprioception was assessed at the hip, knee, and ankle using joint movement sense (JMS), joint position sense (JPS), and dynamic position sense (DPS). Spearman correlations examined relationships between proprioception and gait capacity. RESULTS: Both groups walked slower and took shorter steps under reduced vision; however, children with UMN lesions exhibited larger changes (p < 0.001). In these children, proprioceptive modalities showed weak-to-moderate correlations with gait parameters that strengthened under visual restriction, a pattern observed in pooled analyses. JMS showed the strongest, though weak, correlation with relative walking speed. Joint-specific analyses showed the strongest correlations at the more affected ankle and the less affected hip in children with UMN lesions. CONCLUSION: Children with UMN lesions rely more on proprioceptive input for gait under reduced vision, with the less affected hip and more affected ankle possibly compensating for deficits. Interventions targeting proprioception may enhance walking performance under varying sensory conditions.
